title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Anthropic IPO swell lifts the AI lineup
conditions.summary: Stocks rose to start a big week as Anthropic's IPO filing revived the AI trade and chip stocks rallied. Breadth was about even, with tech doing most of the work ahead of the Fed and megacap earnings.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: S&P 500 rose 0.70% to about 7,677; Nasdaq gained 0.82% to about 26,169.
Dow added 0.28% to about 52,362; Russell 2000 rose about 0.4% to near 2,787.
Anthropic's IPO filing for a Nasdaq listing revived the AI trade.
Chips led, with the PHLX semiconductor index up more than 3%.
Tech, consumer discretionary and industrials led; communications, staples and health care lagged.
Breadth was roughly even, with advancers and decliners near a 1-to-1 split.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: No major US economic data was released today.
The 10-year Treasury yield ended near 4.98%, down about 1 basis point.
A $69 billion 2-year note auction drew weak demand.
WTI crude fell about 2% to near $101 on hopes of easing US-Iran tension; gold rose to about $4,030.
The Fed's two-day meeting starts Tuesday, with a hold widely expected Wednesday; the ECB and BoJ also meet this week.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: RRC (Range Resources): +16% — EQT agreed to buy it in an all-stock deal valued above $50 billion.
TSLA (Tesla): +6% — Barclays upgraded it to Overweight with a $450 target.
LITE (Lumentum): +10% — StoneX started coverage with a $1,200 target.
NVDA (Nvidia): +2.4% — chip stocks rebounded with the AI trade.
XP (XP Inc.): about -50% — Brazilian stocks sank after Lula won reelection.
NU (Nu Holdings): about -20% — hit by the same Brazil election selloff.
FICO (Fair Isaac): -8.6% — analyst downgrades over its mortgage score pricing plan.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: Verizon (before the open): EPS beat, revenue missed, and it raised its full-year outlook.
Cadence Design (after the close): beat and raised its 2026 forecast; shares up about 2% after hours.
Celestica (after the close): strong beat on AI data center demand; shares up about 9% after hours.
Whirlpool (after the close): surprise loss and lower outlook; shares down about 8% after hours.
Amkor (after the close): slight miss but shares up about 5% after hours.

sections.title: Business News
items: Anthropic filed for a US IPO under the ticker ANT, with first-half revenue of $16.3 billion.
Meta plans to raise up to $95 billion to fund AI infrastructure, starting with $35 billion in stock.
DoorDash slipped on a report it is in advanced talks to buy Instacart.
The FTC and 20 states sued Dollar General over alleged overcharging.
Four banks lined up financing for Broadcom custom AI chips for Anthropic.

sections.title: On Deck
items: 7:30 AM CT: Durable goods orders (forecast +1.8%).
9:00 AM CT: Consumer confidence (forecast 80.5) and new home sales.
Before the open: Coca-Cola, Boeing, UPS, PayPal, Novartis.
After the close: Visa, Robinhood, Seagate, NXP Semiconductors.
Fed meeting begins; no Fed speeches during the meeting.

Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Monday, October twenty-sixth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Sunset Session, the full wrap of today's market. The sun is sliding down into the water, the last set of the day is rolling in, and I'm already waxing the board for tomorrow. Gus the wonder dog spent the afternoon chasing sand crabs, and now he's back on his towel for the wrap. Give the Trade Wind surfers a sunset hello, Gus! [BARK]

Here's the final set. Stocks caught a clean wave to start the week. The S and P five hundred rose seven tenths of a percent to about seven thousand six hundred seventy-seven. The Nasdaq gained eight tenths of a percent to about twenty-six thousand one hundred sixty-nine. The Dow added about three tenths of a percent to roughly fifty-two thousand three hundred sixty, and small caps rose about four tenths of a percent. The big swell was Anthropic filing for its initial public offering. That's one huge grommet paddling out, and it lit up the A I trade. Chip stocks led, with the semiconductor index up more than three percent. Health care and staples lagged. Breadth was close to even, so this was a tech led ride.

Wind and weather. There was no major economic data today. The ten year Treasury yield ended near four point nine eight percent, off about a basis point. Crude oil slipped about two percent to near one hundred one dollars, on hopes of easing tension with Iran. Gold rose to around four thousand thirty dollars. The VIX dropped to around eighteen. The Fed starts its two day meeting tomorrow, and markets expect a hold on Wednesday.

The lineup. Range Resources rode a monster wave, up nearly sixteen percent after E Q T agreed to buy it in a deal worth more than fifty billion dollars. Gus, that's worth a biscuit! Here you go, buddy! [SNACK] Tesla gained about six percent after a Barclays upgrade. Nvidia, the Kahuna of chips, rose more than two percent. On the wipeout side, Brazilian stocks got gnarly after the presidential runoff. X P fell about fifty percent.

Tide chart. Verizon beat on earnings but missed on revenue this morning. After the close, Cadence Design beat and raised its forecast, up about two percent late. Whirlpool sank about eight percent after a surprise loss.

Beach talk. Meta plans to raise up to ninety five billion dollars for A I buildout. DoorDash slipped on a report that it's in talks to buy Instacart. And the F T C and twenty states sued Dollar General over alleged overcharging.

Tomorrow's forecast. Durable goods orders hit at seven thirty A M Central. Consumer confidence and new home sales follow at nine A M Central. Coca-Cola, Boeing, U P S and PayPal report before the open. Visa, Robinhood and Seagate report after the close. And no Fed speeches, since the meeting is underway. Catch the Dawn Patrol tomorrow morning.

This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
